note: Jobs to be done, in the buyer's words, mapped to the outcome pathway they belong to. From the Grace Hill JTBD working session. A job is what someone is trying to accomplish — not a feature, not a persona.
formula: When [situation], I need to [motivation], so I can [outcome].

jobs.job: When regulations or risks arise, I need to make sure the whole organization is compliant — and be able to prove it.
jobs.pain: They can show training was assigned. They cannot show who was taught what, on which version, and when.
jobs.outcome: An audit trail per employee per policy version, produced in minutes rather than days.

jobs.job: When the business needs consistency, I define how teams should operate and make sure it is followed.
jobs.pain: The standard exists in a document nobody opens. Following it is optional in practice.
jobs.outcome: One standard that holds at every property, with acknowledgment evidence behind it.

jobs.job: When performance issues arise, I need to work out whether it is skill, process, or effort.
jobs.pain: They guess. The fix is chosen before the cause is known, so it often does not work.
jobs.outcome: A shop shows what was actually said, training closes the gap, the next shop proves it moved.

jobs.job: When a new employee joins, I need them fully operational across every system and expectation.
jobs.pain: Onboarding is paperwork and shadowing. Time to productive is unmeasured and long.
jobs.outcome: Role-based paths assigned automatically, with competency measured rather than attendance.

jobs.job: When managing multiple properties, I need consistency so performance is not dependent on individual teams.
jobs.pain: Performance tracks whichever manager happens to be at that property. It leaves when they do.
jobs.outcome: The same standard everywhere, and visibility into which properties are drifting from it.

jobs.job: When turnover is high, I want better training and development so people stay.
jobs.pain: Replacing an employee costs roughly twice their salary, and the cost lands quietly.
jobs.outcome: Development paths people can see, tied to the work they actually do.

jobs.job: When leasing performance drops, I need to understand why, fast, so I can protect revenue.
jobs.pain: The numbers say conversion fell. Nothing says what changed in the conversation.
jobs.outcome: See the prospect experience directly, and fix the part that broke.

jobs.job: When resident satisfaction declines, I need the drivers so I can improve retention.
jobs.pain: A score with no comparison set and no owner for the fix. Nothing changes after the survey.
jobs.outcome: Benchmarked drivers, and the finding assigned to the person who owns it.

jobs.job: When feedback highlights recurring issues, I want to turn them into training.
jobs.pain: Feedback and training live in different systems, so the loop never closes.
jobs.outcome: A recurring theme becomes a course assignment without leaving the platform.

jobs.job: When reviewing feedback, I want clear prioritisation so I focus on what moves the most.
jobs.pain: Everything is flagged, so nothing is prioritized. Teams triage by whoever complained loudest.
jobs.outcome: Ranked by impact on renewal intention, not by volume of comments.

jobs.job: When performance varies across properties, I need to know where to invest so I can improve NOI.
jobs.pain: Investment goes where attention goes, not where return is highest.
jobs.outcome: Property performance against real comps, so spend follows the gap.

jobs.job: When evaluating a new portfolio, I need to assess team capability and risk before I own the problem.
jobs.pain: Diligence covers the asset. Nobody diligences the people running it.
jobs.outcome: A capability and compliance baseline before the transition, not after.

source: Grace Hill Jobs to be Done working session, August 2026, mapped to the RML outcome pathways.
